subject: Load profile & POC qualification — next steps and sample traffic
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Load profile & POC qualification — next steps and sample traffic

Hi Amit — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap of what we captured in the call and proposed next steps to get the POC running: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary use: in-product summarization and QA for patient intake forms (batch and realtime).
- Expected baseline traffic pattern: daytime steady-state with short bursts at shift changes (08:00 and 16:00 local).
- Initial scope: 3 endpoints (summarize_record, redact_pi, short_answer) during PoC.

Key workload profile (please confirm):
- Steady RPS: 6–8 req/s (avg 1.1–1.3k tokens per request)
- Peak bursts: up to 45 req/s for ~2–5 minutes (token length distribution skewed higher for full intake PDFs ~3–4k tokens for batch jobs)
- Concurrency target for latency SLO: 20 concurrent requests (95th pct <= 450ms token-latency objective)
- Typical request types: streaming for summarization, non-streaming for redaction

Success criteria we propose for the POC (draft):
1) Functionality: output quality within existing thresholds compared to your current baseline prompts (we'll set up a shared prompt/eval sheet).
2) Performance: sustained steady-state throughput at 8 RPS with p95 latency <500ms for short requests; survive burst to 45 RPS with graceful degradation (fallback to reduced model variant).
3) Cost: target token cost reduction >= 25% vs current internal serving by using batching + prefix caching and a quantized variant.
4) Operational: tracing + per-request observability available in Console; audit log access for sample queries.

Immediate next steps
- You: upload a small sample workload CSV with representative request sizes (I attached a template — novus_workload_sample.csv).
- Us: draft a one-page trial plan + timeline and propose reserved windows for traffic injection. See attached redwood-trial-plan-v1.pdf.
- Procurement: if procurement wants standard T&C/PO path, copy procurement@novushealth.com and we will circulate a statement-of-work.

Proposed timeline
- By Jun 2: Novus uploads sample workload + selects two evaluation prompts for summarization.
- Jun 4–9: Redwood config & baseline trial runs in dedicated sandbox environment.
- Jun 10–18: Trial traffic window + joint evaluation.
- Jun 21: Joint readout + decision on expansion.

Can you confirm the workload numbers above (RPS/peak/concurrency) and confirm who will own the sample upload on your side?

Thanks — attaching the trial plan and a small sample template.

—
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182

Attachments: novus_workload_sample.csv (csv), redwood-trial-plan-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Amit Desai <amit@novushealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Load profile & POC qualification — next steps and sample traffic

Thanks Rachel — that summary is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The steady RPS for weekday daytime is closer to 10–12 req/s for the intake endpoint once we include web and mobile clients; the 6–8 I mentioned was conservative. Apologies for the flip.
- Peak bursts can spike to ~60 req/s for 3–4 minutes when multiple clinics sync at shift change.
- Token distribution: median ~900 tokens, 75th ~1.5k, 95th ~3.8k (batch redaction jobs include full documents).
- Concurrency: we currently see up to 28 concurrent long-running jobs during processing windows.

We'll upload the workload CSV by EOD Jun 2. I'll loop in Priya from platform who will own the upload. Priya's email: priya.platform@novushealth.com (cc not included yet).

On success criteria, the cost reduction target is reasonable — we can be flexible if the perf objectives are met. For procurement, we'll confirm PO process by Jun 4.

Appreciate the clear timeline.

—
Amit Desai
Head of Product, Novus Health
amit@novushealth.com

Date: 2027-05-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Load profile & POC qualification — next steps and sample traffic

Thanks Amit — good detail. A couple internal notes and an ask: 

Internal note (for Rachel/Karthik): if Novus steady-state is 10–12 RPS with 60 RPS spikes and concurrency up to 28, we should plan for a dedicated sandbox with the following minimum sizing:
- 2 x A100-ish GPU equivalent (or equivalent multi-GPU pool) for initial trial to meet burst handling and token throughput for long documents.
- Enable KV/prefix caching for repeated patient prompts to reduce token processing for streaming summarization.

Ask for Novus: can you mark which of the sample rows are latency-sensitive (web/mobile) vs batch? We'll use that to tune batching windows and choose streaming vs non-streaming paths. Please include a column "latency_profile" in the upload (values: low/medium/high).

I'll also prepare the canary fallback plan (model variants + automatic routing) and add to the trial plan doc. Rachel — I'll drop an updated redwood-trial-plan-v1.1.pdf into the Drive link by Jun 4.

Best,
Ben
VP, Solutions
